theorems.title: Stop/convergence certificate for the (T, n_e) loop the pipeline actually runs: exact gain, damped-Picard window, 2x2 Gauss-Seidel gate, a-posteriori residual stop
theorems.informal: With IPD off, the pipeline's reduced outer map (SB-graph fit on x* = E + IP(z-1) with element dummies and unit weights; n_e from the sb_offset median element) is affine in u = 1/kT on each median piece, u' = g u + c, with g = (Σ_e b_e D_e) D_m / Σ_e (W_e + b_e D_e²) (INV FI-1; the closed form matched iterative.py to 5 decimals in 4 executed configurations, pipeline_gain.py). Theorems: (a) the λ-damped iterate satisfies u_n - u* = (1-λ+λg)^n (u_0 - u*) exactly, so every start converges iff 1 - 2/λ < g < 1 (λ = 1/2: g ∈ (-3,1)); (b) nonlinear version: if g' ∈ [m,M] ⊂ (1-2/λ, 1) on an invariant box the damped map has a unique attracting fixed point, and a fixed point with g'(T*) > 1 repels for every λ > 0 (damping cannot rescue positive feedback); (c) the real iteration damps T and n_e separately (R9-02 corrected evidence), with Jacobian J = [[1/2+A/2, B/2],[C/2(1/2+A/2), 1/2+BC/4]]: det J = (1+A)/4 and 1 + det J - tr J = (1-g)/4 with g = A + BC, so by the 2x2 Schur-Cohn criterion ρ(J) < 1 iff g < 1 ∧ -5 < A < 3 ∧ 3A + BC > -9 (checked on 2e5 random draws, 0 mismatches); g < 1 is exactly the monotone-divergence boundary; (d) unit-invariant 2-D gate for the existing jointOuterContraction_box: weights w_T, w_n > 0 with max(a + b w_n/w_T, c w_T/w_n + d) < 1 exist iff a < 1 ∧ d < 1 ∧ bc < (1-a)(1-d), which is invariant under rescaling n_e, unlike the current row-sum gate that always fails in eV / cm⁻³ units (PS-10); (e) a-posteriori stop: for a q-Lipschitz map |u - u*| ≤ |Φu - u|/(1-q); for the affine damped map with step s = λ|Φu - u| this is |u - u*| = s/(λ(1-g)), so at g = 0.964 the default 100 K stop step is compatible with ≈5.6 kK linearized distance (INV-02). The existing outerLoop_contracts / outerLoop_contracts_apriori spine is NOT this object: with the consistent Saha offset its composite map is constant (INV-01, proved axiom-clean in scratch ModelBDegenerate.lean), its gate L1·L2 evaluates to 6e3-5e4 on realistic Ti data (INV-03, PS-03), and it models a fixed-R density leg the pipeline does not iterate (PS-04).

def dampedMap (lam : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (u : ℝ) : ℝ := (1 - lam) * u + lam * g u
theorem dampedAffine_iterate (lam g c u0 : ℝ) (hg : g ≠ 1) (n : ℕ) : (dampedMap lam (fun u => g * u + c))^[n] u0 - c / (1 - g) = (1 - lam + lam * g) ^ n * (u0 - c / (1 - g))   -- PROVED (Proofs.lean, axiom-clean)

theorem dampedMap_contracts {g g' : ℝ → ℝ} {a b m M lam : ℝ} (hlam0 : 0 < lam) (hlam1 : lam ≤ 1) (hd : ∀ T ∈ Set.Icc a b, HasDerivAt g (g' T) T) (hmM : ∀ T ∈ Set.Icc a b, m ≤ g' T ∧ g' T ≤ M) (hlo : 1 - 2 / lam < m) (hhi : M < 1) (hmaps : Set.MapsTo (dampedMap lam g) (Set.Icc a b) (Set.Icc a b)) (hab : a ≤ b) : ∃ Tstar ∈ Set.Icc a b, dampedMap lam g Tstar = Tstar ∧ ∀ T0 ∈ Set.Icc a b, Tendsto (fun n => (dampedMap lam g)^[n] T0) atTop (𝓝 Tstar)

theorems.title: IPD gauge and the implicit IPD-aware Saha inverse: exact bias factor, unique root and contraction at rate Δχ/(2kT), log-sensitivity -1/(1-q)
theorems.informal: (a) Gauge: S(χ - d) = S(χ)·e^{d/kT} exactly, so an IPD-off inverse applied to IPD-on data reports n_e·e^{-Δχ/kT}. PS-05 reports that this reproduces R1-07's measured 0.9358x n_e at 1e17 cm⁻³ / 11 kK (auditor's ipd.py with a Debye-Hückel anchor). With an element-independent Δχ on the I→II edge, a line-ratio-only route (sb_offset) identifies only n_e·e^{-Δχ/kT}, and the closure composition is IPD-invariant because a common factor cancels (composition_smul_invariant). Stark or injected n_e routes are biased by exactly e^{Δχ/kT}, so a Stark/Saha pair measures Δχ: ln(n_Stark/n_Saha,IPD-off) = Δχ/kT. (b) Implicit inverse with Δχ = kT·b·√n_e (b abstract): in ℓ = ln n_e the IPD-aware inverse is the fixed point of F(ℓ) = ln a + b e^{ℓ/2}, a = S(χ)/R, and F'(ℓ) = Δχ/(2kT) =: q. There is at most one root with q < 1, since ℓ - F(ℓ) is strictly increasing there. F contracts on every invariant half-line where q ≤ q̄ < 1, so jitpipe's 3-step inner IPD loop has error ≤ q̄³ (≈3e-5 at 1e17). Roots fold at q = 1, near 9e19 cm⁻³ at 11 kK. (c) d ln n_e / d ln R = -1/(1-q), which replaces electronDensity_relativeError's exact -1 in an IPD-on context.

theorems.title: Refuse-to-report policy theorem: certified abstention on the Aitchison PAS loss, with the proof that a tautological diagnostic cannot be a refusal reason
theorems.informal: Let ℓ_i be per-spectrum Aitchison losses with certified bounds L_i ≤ ℓ_i ≤ U_i. (a) If the policy answers iff U_i ≤ λ, then PAS_gated ≤ N·λ, so it never does worse than refusing everything. (b) Its regret against the oracle policy (answer iff ℓ_i < λ) is at most the sum over the ambiguous set {L_i ≤ λ < U_i} of (U_i - L_i). (c) If it refuses only when L_i > λ, then G = PAS_forced - PAS_gated ≥ 0 on every data set, which is SC-04's gate-value requirement. (d) Loss certificate: for positive compositions, d_A(Ĉ, C) ≤ ‖e - c·1‖₂ for every c, where e_s = ln(N̂_s/N_s). Common-mode errors (Fcal, closure scale, oxide normalization) cancel exactly (FT-07), so U_i is computable from per-species log-error bounds alone. (e) Refusal-reason soundness: on the sb_offset route the Saha-consistency residual R̂·n̂_e - S(T) is identically 0 (overhaul TS-01), and the Saha temperature equals the fitted one whenever S/R̂ is injective in T. A reason that is constant in the data carries no information, which formally grounds marking that criterion not_evaluated on that route.

theorems.informal: Lines are grouped by element e and carry weights w > 0. theorems.title: Partition-function truncation and cutoff policy: tail bound, strictly T-dependent policy ratio that no gA factor can absorb, and the continuity constraint on an n_e-dependent cutoff
theorems.informal: Let U_cut sum only the levels with E < cut. (i) 0 ≤ U - U_cut ≤ (Σ_{E ≥ cut} g)·e^{-cut/kT}. (ii) If at least one level is kept and one dropped, U/U_cut is strictly increasing in T: every dropped level lies above every kept level, so d ln(U/U_cut)/dβ < 0. No extra ordering hypothesis is needed for a sharp cutoff (the plasma-state auditor's extra hypothesis is redundant). (iii) Hence no T-independent c satisfies U = c·U_cut for all T. A change of cutoff policy therefore cannot be absorbed by the calibration layer's T-independent gA corrections, which is the formal content of R1-02's 'T-dependent ~5% Al I bias that gA corrections cannot absorb'. (iv) population and the Boltzmann plot are invariant under truncation only if the numerator and U use the same list (conventions.md prose made a theorem). (v) With a sharp n_e-dependent cutoff cut(n_e) = χ - Δχ(n_e), U jumps whenever a level crosses. That falsifies every Lipschitz-in-n_e hypothesis of jointOuterContraction_box and C9-C11 (two-level witness). Only a continuous occupation-weight policy w_k(n_e) ∈ [0,1] is compatible with the spec's contraction theorems, which is a formal constraint on R1-02's LevelCutoffPolicy decision.

theorems.title: Aitchison error transfer and abundance-scaled closure bounds: perturbation and scale invariance, aliasing loss = ‖clr ρ‖, relative-error dichotomy
theorems.informal: (i) clr(a⊙x) = clr a + clr x. Hence d_A is perturbation-invariant (mole↔mass with a = atomic masses) and scale-invariant (the oxide closure output is a positive multiple of the mole closure). (ii) Aliasing: if N̂_s = N_s·ρ_s, as for the classic reader under wrong atomic data or response, then d_A(N̂, N) = ‖clr ρ‖, independent of N, and a common factor in ρ is invisible (this is the calibration gauge). (iii) Relative closure bound: if |N̂_s - N_s| ≤ η N_s for all s with η < 1, then |Ĉ_s - C_s| ≤ 2η/(1-η)·C_s for every s, whatever the abundance. For a 0.5% minor with a 5% error this gives 5.26e-4, against 5.23e-4 actual and the repo's absolute bound of 0.0557 (LIT-05). An additive-error witness shows amplification on minors, so 'closure amplifies minor-element errors' holds only for additive error components. (iv) The relative bound transfers unchanged to mass fractions, via composition of M⊙N.

theorems.title: Closure-free ratio mode vs NeutralityScale: normalization invariance, and the exact ΔIP stage-fraction sensitivity that decides when |ΔE_k - ΔIP| pair matching is right
theorems.informal: (a) Ratio mode is invariant under every common-mode normalization: the ratios of composition(c·N) are N_a/N_b, and the closure-normalized and neutrality-normalized readers (Alt.closureEstimate, and the per-unit intensities divided by Alt.neutralityScale) return identical ratios, even with an undetected species. NeutralityScale is already proved (it recovers the absolute Fcal from a Stark n_e) but is orthogonal to ratio mode: it cannot improve a ratio, and its own bias is the undetected charge share. (b) The ratio-mode error channel is the stage fraction. For neutral lines and two-stage totals N_tot = n_I(1 + S/n_e), the log-ratio evaluated at an assumed β̂ has exact β-derivative (E_a - ⟨E⟩_{I,A}) - (E_b - ⟨E⟩_{I,B}) - f_A κ_A + f_B κ_B, where κ_X = χ_X + 3/(2β) + ⟨E⟩_{II,X} - ⟨E⟩_{I,X} and f_X = ρ_X/(1+ρ_X) is the ionized fraction. When both elements are mostly ionized (f → 1) this reduces to (E_a - E_b) - (χ_A - χ_B) - (⟨E⟩_{II,A} - ⟨E⟩_{II,B}). So BL-48's |ΔE_k - ΔIP| rule nulls the first-order T-sensitivity exactly when the ion-stage mean excitation energies also match (its 'plus partition slopes'). When both are mostly neutral the right rule is E-matching plus U-slope matching. For intermediate or unequal f neither rule is optimal, and the full coefficient is the selection objective. (c) Two-point bound on a β-box: |Δ(β̂) - Δ(β)| ≤ L·|β̂ - β|, with L the box supremum of the coefficient.

theorems.title: Energy-affine atomic-data gauge: an E-linear gA error is exactly a temperature shift (calibration-layer non-identifiability)
theorems.informal: If ln(A_k/A'_k) = α + b·E_k, the Boltzmann-plot slope built with A' is exactly -1/(kT) + b and the residuals are unchanged. The data are therefore observationally identical to true data at 1/(kT') = 1/(kT) - b plus an intercept shift. With per-spectrum free T and Fcal, the E-linear component of a global per-line correction δ_l cannot be identified within one stage and one U family. Across species and stages it leaks only through U_s(T')/U_s(T) and the Saha T-terms, which FT-15 bounds. W3-C's designed gauges (per-species median δ = 0, one response point per instrument) do not fix this direction, and the overhaul's named design risk (the layer absorbing misspecification such as two-emitter mixing) lives in it.

theorems.title: Information floor for the Boltzmann slope and the log-ratio: heteroscedastic Aitken BLUE and the common-slope intercept-difference variance (a BLUE floor, not a Cramér-Rao theorem)
theorems.informal: (a) Deterministic Aitken core: among linear unbiased weights (Σa = 0, Σa·E = 1), the WLS weights w_k(E_k - Ē_w)/SS_w minimize Σa²σ² with σ_k² = 1/w_k, and the minimum equals 1/Σ w(E - Ē_w)². (b) Probabilistic form: under uncorrelated noise with Var ε_k = σ_k², WLS is BLUE with that variance, and unweighted OLS can be arbitrarily worse. Adding one noisy line can raise the OLS variance: with E = (0,1,2) and σ² = (1,1,10⁴), the variance goes from 2 to 2500.25. So FisherLineSelection's 'adding a line never hurts' holds only for WLS or homoscedastic noise. (c) Log-ratio floor: for two species with separate intercepts and a shared slope, d̂ = b̂_a - b̂_b has variance σ²(1/n_a + 1/n_b + (Ē_a - Ē_b)²/(SS_a + SS_b)) and is BLUE, so the line-level precision of ln(N_a/N_b) is limited by the mismatch of mean upper energies. This is the best-linear-unbiased floor. The Cramér-Rao inequality over all estimators is NOT proved: mathlib has no Fisher information (FM-13), and FisherLineSelection's crlb_slope defines the Fisher information rather than deriving it.

Then the source function ε/κ = B0/(e^x - 1), free of N, U, A and L. (ii) With a Kirchhoff source, the emergent integrated intensity S·W_ψ(κL) is strictly increasing in L and in N. (iii) At fixed n_l, the peak τ0 ∝ n_l·L/width falls strictly as the Stark width grows. This is the BL-45 acceptance identity and restores the factor R3-05 found the pipeline drops. (v) Transfer before instrument: for a probability kernel R, equivWidth φ τ ≤ equivWidth (R⋆φ) τ. theorems.informal: Let G(x) = Σ Ntot_s S_s/(x + S_s) have fixed point r > 0. theorems.title: Ion apparent temperature ≥ neutral apparent temperature in a line-of-sight mixture (Saha reweighting of the tilted mean)
theorems.informal: Consider a positive mixture of LTE zones at uniform n_e. Ion-stage zone weights equal the neutral weights times ρ_z = S(T_z)/n_e, the partition functions cancel, and ρ is antitone in b_z = 1/(kT_z). A reweighting that is antitone in b lowers the tilted mean inverse temperature at any anchor, and tiltMean is antitone in the anchor. So if the ion pair's lower line energy is at least the neutral pair's upper line energy, then β_app(ion) ≤ β_app(neutral), i.e. T_app(ion) ≥ T_app(neutral). This is the sign Aguilera & Aragón measured (9890 K neutral vs 11400 K ion). The multi-stage collapse (Cσ master line, pooled SB-graph slope, saha_joint_identifiability's single T) therefore mixes two different tilted means.

theorems.informal: (a) Sufficient criterion: if the COG log-slope τW'(τ)/W(τ) is strictly decreasing on (0,∞), then for every r > 1 the pair ratio n ↦ W_ψ(rn)/W_ψ(n) is strictly antitone. For a single fixed r the converse is false, since ε may oscillate with period ln r. (b) Counterexample: take the two-step profile ψ = 1_[0,1] + η·1_[0,M], a strong core plus a weak broad wing. Then W(τ) = (1 - e^{-τ(1+η)}) + (M - 1)(1 - e^{-τη}). With η = 1/100, M = 20 and r = 2, the ratio is 1.508, 1.391 and 1.583 at n = 1, 3 and 10 (computed this session), so it is not injective: ratios just above 1.391 are attained at two column densities. (c) Pre-registered conjecture, numerics only (LF-04): the Voigt pair ratio is two-branched for γ/σ from 0.01 to 0.93, inside the W3-B gate range τ 0.1-30, while the pure Lorentzian ratio is monotone (from r down to √r). Consequence: C13, cogRatio_injOn and doubletRatio_injOn certify uniqueness only for the flat kernel.
